name: Reply.io
description: Reply.io is an AI-powered sales-engagement platform for contacts, multichannel sequences, email and LinkedIn outreach, inbox workflows, calls, SMS, WhatsApp, tasks, scheduling, enrichment, automation, and reporting.
agentUseSummary: Add a customer-owned dedicated read-scoped V3 API key and one exact positive numeric sequence ID. Agents may read only the bound sequence's privacy-redacted name, creation time, native status, and archive flag. Relay excludes owners, teams, sending accounts, schedules, steps/content, contacts, messages, AI SDR, enrichment, reports, webhooks, administration, mutations, raw REST/MCP/CLI, polling, bulk work, downloads, and exports.

capabilities.label: Read sequence status
capabilities.description: Read one bounded privacy-redacted status summary for the exact configured Reply.io sequence ID.

approvalRequired.label: Read sequence status

blocked.label: Change or run sequences
blocked.description: Creating, updating, archiving, deleting, starting, pausing, scheduling, sequencing, or changing sending accounts and settings is outside V1.

blocked.label: Access people or messages
blocked.description: Contacts, lists, email addresses, LinkedIn profiles, inboxes, replies, calls, SMS, WhatsApp, tasks, sends, and person-level state are outside V1.

blocked.label: Read private sequence content
blocked.description: Team and owner IDs, sending-account IDs, schedules, steps, subjects, bodies, templates, variants, attachments, settings, and raw responses are never returned.

blocked.label: Access AI or administration
blocked.description: AI SDR, enrichment, email validation, custom fields, blacklists, accounts, users, holiday calendars, reports, webhooks, background jobs, and administration are outside V1.

blocked.label: Call raw or bulk surfaces
blocked.description: Raw REST, MCP, CLI, OpenAPI pass-through, arbitrary endpoints, list/search/filter queries, pagination, polling, imports, bulk work, downloads, exports, and crawling are outside V1.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: The bounded private sequence status read requires matching approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The selected status read runs without Relay approval while exact sequence binding, fixed endpoint, audit, redaction, and response bounds remain enforced; people, messaging, sequence writes, AI, and administration stay blocked.

providerSetup.blocker: No customer-owned Reply.io account, active subscription, dedicated read-scoped V3 API key, exact preconfigured sequence ID, or live endpoint-auth acceptance evidence is available in this workspace.
providerSetup.nextAction: In the provider-console task create a dedicated V3 key limited to the exact read authority required by Reply's current key controls, choose one preconfigured sequence, record its exact numeric ID, store both through Relay, then validate the endpoint's X-API-Key contract, sequence binding, privacy redaction, approval/denial, rate-limit handling, key rotation, disconnect, and post-disconnect denial without changing or running the sequence.

evidence.supports: Official V3 introduction documents a broad full-product REST surface spanning contacts, sequences, inbox, scheduling, reports, webhooks, and background work.

Official endpoint reference documents fixed GET https://api.reply.io/v3/sequences/{id}, X-API-Key authentication, positive numeric ID, and a response containing safe status fields plus private owners, team, sending accounts, settings, schedules, steps, subjects, and message bodies.

Official authentication guide documents dashboard-created API keys, key secrecy, availability controls, and permissions; live setup must confirm the sequence endpoint's declared key-header contract during acceptance.

Official product page documents scoped independent V3 API keys, revocation, 270-plus endpoints, per-minute/hour limits, OAuth, webhooks, async jobs, MCP, and broad contacts/enrichment/sequence capabilities.
Official DPA identifies uploaded personal data including full names, email addresses, phone numbers, and positions, reinforcing V1 exclusion of person-level data.
